canonical_statement: The study prospectively evaluated whether activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) monitoring during continuous intravenous heparin therapy was associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism or bleeding.
Two hundred thirty-four patients receiving continuous intravenous heparin were studied; 162 were treated for venous thromboembolism and 72 were treated for other diseases.

canonical_statement: Recurrent venous thrombosis was diagnosed when new-site symptoms and signs developed or when pain persisted at the original thrombosis site; pulmonary embolism required new compatible symptoms or signs with or without new chest imaging or lung-scan lesions.

canonical_statement: Bleeding was assessed by daily interview and observation of apparent blood loss and transfusion requirements; bleeding was major if blood transfusion was required and minor if treatment was not needed.

canonical_statement: APTT was measured on citrated platelet-poor plasma using kaolin, a three-minute incubation before recalcification, and phospholipid; pooled normal plasma APTT in the laboratory was 39-41 seconds.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that recurrent venous thromboembolism during heparin treatment was rare when heparin was adjusted to keep APTT at or above 1.5 times the control value.

exposures.details: Continuous intravenous heparin infusion; initial 5,000-U bolus followed by maintenance infusion.

canonical_statement: The study relied partly on clinical diagnosis of venous thrombosis, which the authors acknowledged was imprecise and could produce false-positive and false-negative results; clinically silent emboli may also have been missed.
The heparin-dose adjustment recommendation was followed to a variable extent, so observed APTT exposure was not produced by a strictly controlled dosing protocol.
Only five recurrent venous thromboembolic events occurred, limiting precision and making causal interpretation of the APTT-recurrence association uncertain.

The authors explicitly stated that the study did not prove the five recurrent thromboembolic events would have been prevented if sufficient heparin had been given to maintain APTT within the recommended therapeutic range.
The authors recommended giving enough heparin to prolong APTT to between 1.5 and 2.5 times the control level at all times in patients with venous thromboembolism.

exposures.details: Continuous intravenous heparin infusion; initial 5,000-U bolus followed by maintenance infusion.

canonical_statement: The authors described the 1.5-2.5-times-control APTT regimen as safe and effective but noted that bleeding complications could not be avoided even within this APTT range, especially in postoperative patients.

exposures.details: Continuous intravenous heparin infusion; initial 5,000-U bolus followed by maintenance infusion.
